dial.summary: Global M2 upgraded to supportive as the 4-week trend confirms expansion to $103.7T (Aug 2026 G4 aggregate), providing a stealth liquidity tailwind; DXY at 102.19 and real yields at 2.91% remain active headwinds, and the 2s10s curve has flattened to neutral — today's September CPI print (8:30 AM ET, Cleveland Fed nowcast 3.60% YoY) is the binary catalyst: a miss below 3.2% could reprice DXY below 100, validate the M2 tailwind, and unlock the next BTC accumulation leg from near $82K.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: MacroMicro G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) confirmed at $103,662.82B for August 2026 (prior reading $102,638.09B for July 2026); 4-week trend UP (+$1,024B, +1.0% MoM) — status upgraded to supportive per scoring rule (supportive if 4-week trend is up); US M2 at $23.34T for August (FRED H.6, next release Oct 27 for September data); no September G4 aggregate yet (6–8 week lag); next full G4 update expected mid-November 2026.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: September 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI = 54.5% (released Oct 1, 2026; August 54.6%, 4-week change −0.1pp within flat threshold); consensus had been 55.0% (slight miss per ForexFactory); New Orders growing, Production growing, Employment growing, Prices Paid 77.9% (multi-year high); status neutral — above 50 but not rising on 4-week basis; October PMI data not yet available; next release November 2, 2026.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY spot at ~102.19 (Oct 13 close per Dealplexus/FXStreet; day range 102.16–102.57); pulled back from the 18-month high of ~102.58 hit Oct 13 on Iran/Russia risk premium; 4-week trend UP from ~99.90 on Sep 13 to 102.19 (+2.3%); status headwind (above 100 threshold); September CPI due today at 8:30 AM ET (consensus 3.6–3.7% YoY) — a miss below 3.2% is the trigger for DXY break below 100 and status improvement.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: 10-year TIPS real yield at 2.91% as of October 9, 2026 (Federal Reserve H.15 release Oct 13; Oct 8 FRED DFII10 = 2.87%); 4-week trend UP from ~2.52% on Sep 9 (+39bps); status headwind (rising on 4-week basis and well above 2% threshold); 10-year breakeven at 2.33% (FRED T10YIE, Oct 9); today's September CPI is the key repricing catalyst — a dovish print could compress real yields meaningfully.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: October 13, 2026: 10Y ~5.21%, 2Y ~4.79% → spread = +42bps (Treasury par-yield data); 4-week trend FLAT (Sep 9 ~42bps → Oct 13 42bps = 0bps change); status downgraded to neutral — curve remains positively sloped but is no longer steepening on a 4-week basis; prior week cluster of 44–47bps (Oct 8–9) suggests modest recent flattening; FOMC Oct 27–28 is the next major curve catalyst.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL at $6,747,560M ($6.748T) for week ending October 7, 2026 (H.4.1 released Oct 8; prior week $6,743,031M = +$4.5B WoW); 4-week trend flat: Sep 9 ~$6,737B → Oct 7 $6,748B = +$11B (+0.16%); status supportive (flat at post-QT-pause stabilization plateau); next H.4.1 release October 15, 2026, covering week ending October 14.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC weighted 8h perp funding rate at ~0.0047% as of October 8, 2026 (MacroMicro); 30-day trend DOWN from 0.0067% on Sep 30 to 0.0047% on Oct 8; Kraken CF perpetual benchmark annualized at 7.5% (Sep 29); BTC spot ~$81,800 (Oct 8, MacroMicro) with BTC.D at 59.3%; status supportive (well below 0.04% overheating threshold — near-zero funding confirms spot-driven accumulation, not leveraged speculation).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$288.67B (Oct 10, 2026 estimate) vs total crypto ~$2.9T → stablecoin dominance ~10.0%; BTC dominance 59.3% (tv-hub.org, Oct 2026); USDT ~$183–184B (63–64% of stablecoin total); 30-day trend DOWN from ~10.5% (Sep 12) to ~10.0% (Oct 10); status supportive — falling stablecoin dominance alongside a rising total market cap confirms active capital rotation into crypto assets.

upcoming.title: PPI (September 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Producer Price Index for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — pipeline inflation released the day after CPI; consensus: +0.5% MoM (vs +0.4% prior); ISM Prices Paid at 77.9% is a leading upside signal; a hot PPI following a hot CPI would reinforce October hike expectations and sustain DXY above 102; a soft print would reinforce any dovish CPI narrative.

upcoming.title: Retail Sales (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Retail Sales for September 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — following the September NFP (+29K), a weak retail sales print would confirm broad consumer softening and reinforce Fed hold narrative; a strong print alongside weak labor extends the late-cycle bifurcation signal; provides pre-FOMC context on Q3 consumer demand ahead of the October 29 GDP advance estimate.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended October 11, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for the week ended October 11, 2026 — released alongside September PPI and Retail Sales; claims trajectory directly informs FOMC odds for the October 27–28 meeting; a print above 200K would reinforce labor market softening following the September NFP of +29K.

upcoming.title: Fed Balance Sheet H.4.1 (week ended October 14, 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve H.4.1 weekly balance sheet release at 4:30 PM ET — covers week ending October 14, 2026; prior reading $6,747,560M ($6.748T, week ending Oct 7); four consecutive weeks of flat-to-marginal expansion; a shift toward contraction combined with rising overnight rates would flip status from supportive to headwind.

upcoming.title: Industrial Production & Capacity Utilization (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Federal Reserve Board releases September 2026 Industrial Production and Capacity Utilization at 9:15 AM ET; completes the Q3 output picture ahead of the GDP advance estimate (October 29); September ISM Manufacturing at 54.5% and Production sub-index growing suggest solid output; a miss would reinforce stagflation risk (hot prices, softening activity) into the October 27–28 FOMC.

upcoming.title: Housing Starts & Building Permits (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau releases September 2026 Housing Starts and Building Permits at 8:30 AM ET; with real yields at 2.91% and mortgage rates elevated, continuation of monthly declines would underscore the drag from high financing costs on housing; provides incremental Q3 residential investment data ahead of the October 29 GDP advance estimate.
